tldr: DISCOVERYWORLD is introduced as the first virtual environment for benchmarking AI agents' ability to perform complete end-to-end cycles of novel scientific discovery, with 120 tasks across 8 diverse topics showing that strong baseline agents significantly lag behind human scientists.
contributions: First virtual environment for benchmarking general scientific discovery ability
Comprehensive evaluation set of 120 tasks spanning 8 themes with 3 difficulty levels and parametric variations
Automatic evaluation framework with three metrics: task completion, task-relevant actions, and discovered explanatory knowledge
Baseline results demonstrating contemporary agents struggle with end-to-end discovery even though they handle component skills moderately well
methods: DISCOVERYWORLD is implemented as a custom simulation engine in Python/Pygame (~20K lines) providing a 32×32 tile grid environment with 14 action types and text/visual observations via JSON. The benchmark includes 120 discovery tasks (8 themes × 3 difficulty levels × 5 random seeds) plus 10 unit test themes, where each task requires agents to form hypotheses, design and run experiments, analyze results, and act on conclusions. Three baseline agents (ReAct, Plan+Exec, and Hypothesizer) were evaluated in a zero-shot setting using GPT-4O, alongside 11 human scientists with MSC or PhD qualifications in natural sciences.
results: Human scientists achieved an average task completion rate of 66% and knowledge score of 55%. In contrast, the best-performing agent (ReAct) completed only 38% of easy tasks and 18% of challenge tasks, while the best knowledge-discovering agent (Hypothesizer) found only 34% of gold knowledge on easy tasks and 8% on challenge tasks. Agents scored 60%+ on unit tests covering component skills like instrument measurement, indicating competence in individual discovery steps but inability to perform end-to-end discovery.
limitations: The 120-task benchmark uses only 5 random seeds per theme/difficulty combination due to evaluation cost. Agents were evaluated in zero-shot with no prior exposure to DISCOVERYWORLD and no carry-over knowledge between tasks. Current environments exercise only systematic search components of discovery, while DISCOVERYWORLD aims for the full pipeline but remains text-based with optional 2D visualization. Even expert human scientists found challenge tasks difficult, with some solved by only a single participant.
